findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as a Git argument
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax (for example, `HEAD; whoami`), `exec` passes it through the platform shell and executes the appended command with the caller's privileges. The base implementation used `execFile("git", ["show", branch])`, which treated the value only as an argument; retain that argument-based invocation (or otherwise avoid shell interpretation).

findings.title: [P2] Keep cancellation attached to the Git process
findings.body: On platforms where `exec` launches Git beneath a shell (notably Windows), callers that cancel the returned `ChildProcess` can terminate only the shell while `git show` continues running. The previous `execFile` return value represented Git directly, so this changes the exported function's cancellation/resource-ownership behavior even for safe branch names.
